request.song: As Good As I Once Was

original.guitar: Nashville session players (not credited in the sources found)
original.amp: Not documented. Mid-2000s Nashville country: Tele into a Fender/Vox-style amp, Marshall-style crunch for choruses
original.effects: Compressor, slapback, spring reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: Single from Honkytonk University (May 2005), produced by James Stroud and Toby Keith. No source documents the guitar gear.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the verses: clean with a little edge when you dig in. Channel B for the choruses: Plexi-style crunch. Mute the strings with your picking hand on the verse rhythm to keep it tight.
recipes.why: Mid-2000s country hits use a clean, compressed Tele sound in the verses and switch to a Marshall-style crunch for the choruses. A short slapback and a little spring reverb tie both channels together.

request.song: As Good As I Once Was

original.guitar: Nashville session players (not credited in the sources found)
original.amp: Not documented. Mid-2000s Nashville country lead: Tele into an EL84 amp at the edge of breakup
original.effects: Compressor, slapback, spring reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: Single from Honkytonk University (May 2005), produced by James Stroud and Toby Keith. No source documents the guitar gear.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the signature riff and the fills, channel B for the solo. The compressor adds sustain to the bends. Hybrid-pick and snap the strings for the chicken-pickin' parts. Roll the guitar volume to 8 if the riff gets too hairy.
recipes.why: A Tele through an EL84 amp at the edge of breakup, compressed for sustain, with a slapback that doubles each note: the classic 2000s Nashville lead sound.
